# John Heymans

> Belgian Olympic 5000m finalist and keynote speaker. Two years after deciding to try, he ran the Olympic 5000m final, on a race schedule chosen by an algorithm he built, against the advice of his federation, his coach and his fellow competitors. The result was the fastest rise up the world rankings in his event's history. His 30-minute keynote turns that story into five lessons for teams.

## The keynote

- Length: 30 minutes, with optional Q&A.
- Languages: English, Dutch or French.
- Format: in person, on a main stage or around a table.
- Settings: conferences and business fairs (1,000+ delegates), company events (100+), executive offsites (20 to 50 senior leaders), leadership dinners (8 to 20).

## The five lessons

1. Your environment sets your ceiling. And consistency beats hard work. (Training in Iten, Kenya, at 2,400 m.)
2. The edge is where the consensus isn't. Don't be afraid to challenge the status quo. (The algorithm that chose his races.)
3. Focus on what you can control. And stop overthinking what you can't. (Setbacks on the way to qualifying.)
4. Embrace the pressure. It comes with the moments that matter. (The Olympic village.)
5. Dare to dream big. Your dreams set your ceiling. (The Olympic final, with "Hey mom, made it" written on his arms.)
